title: The same assessments appear in two files with different coverage
measurement: 18269 (prompt, annotator) pairs appear in both files; 0 disagree on the world ranking. Present only in comparisons: 0. Only in annotators: 293.

title: Some annotators submit the identical ranking string on every prompt they saw
measurement: 994 annotators with 5 or more rankings; 6 give the SAME ranking string every time (0.6%). Example counts: [5, 5, 5, 5, 20]
falsifier: zero annotators with a constant ranking across five or more prompts

title: Rationale reuse and very short rationales indicate low-effort responding
measurement: 1012 annotators wrote 18657 world rationales; 8 reuse the same text for at least two thirds of their prompts; 3045 rationales (16.3%) are under 20 characters
falsifier: no annotator reusing rationales and no rationale under 20 characters

title: A small tail of criteria uses the evaluative vocabulary the onboarding quiz taught annotators to avoid -- the quiz mostly worked
measurement: 15248 criteria; 433 (2.8%) contain an explicitly evaluative word such as good, better, appropriate or helpful, which the quiz drilled as the marker of a SUBJECTIVE criterion; 100 (0.7%) open with a generic quality adjective rather than anything prompt-specific

title: Very short criteria are unlikely to be checkable against a response
CHECKED: the position effect is statistically real but worth essentially NOTHING on the metric everything here uses
measurement: a fixed score vector derived from corpus-wide first-place frequencies, applied identically to all 18678 rankings, reaches pairwise concordance 0.4993 against a chance level of 0.5000 -- a difference of -0.0007. Wave one measured the slot effect at chi-square 74.4 on first place and 220.7 on last, both far past p=.001. Both are true: at n=16,530 a tiny asymmetry is overwhelmingly significant AND carries no predictive power. Wave one called this BLOCKING; on this evidence that was wrong.
falsifier: a slot-only predictor departing from 0.5000 by more than 0.01

title: CHECKED: importance is not degenerate
measurement: 3 distinct values over 18678 assessments; the modal answer holds 50.0%. Modal value: Very important (serious impact if wrong)

title: CHECKED: subjectivity is not degenerate
measurement: 4 distinct values over 18678 assessments; the modal answer holds 46.8%. Modal value: The correct answer depends on a person's values or culture

title: CHECKED: representativeness is not degenerate
measurement: 5 distinct values over 18678 assessments; the modal answer holds 41.0%. Modal value: It is 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗮𝘁 𝗮𝗹𝗹 likely that I would ask a question like this to an AI
